NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a thermal-gradient-driven reconfiguration of the balancing schedule to prevent series string imbalance drift. Standard practice uses a fixed balancing schedule independent of thermal conditions; this intervention continuously adjusts balancing based on real-time temperature measurements to counteract thermal-induced capacity fade and self-discharge variations. The closest existing practice is temperature-dependent charge rate adjustment in EV batteries, but this is novel as it applies thermal-aware balancing specifically to counteract thermal-gradient-induced imbalance in stationary storage. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by equalizing the electrochemical aging rate across cells through localized balancing that compensates for temperature-dependent degradation.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the Arrhenius equation for degradation rate: k = A·exp(-Ea/RT). A 15°C gradient across cells at 40°C average creates a ~20% difference in degradation rates. By balancing more aggressively in warmer cells (higher degradation rate) and less in cooler cells, the intervention equalizes the effective aging rate. A 1 A balancing current can transfer ~0.36 C/hour; over a 10-year life, this can compensate for up to ~7% capacity difference, sufficient to maintain <35 mV spread.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (a) BMS logic modification: Add temperature-weighted balancing algorithm to existing BMS software (replaces fixed schedule)
- (b) Commercial temperature sensor array: Install 13 NTC thermocouples (one per cell), commercially available temperature sensors
- (c) Balancing current schedule parameter: Set balancing current multiplier as a function of cell temperature (0.8× at 35°C, 1.2× at 45°C)
- (a) Thermal mapping routine: Add to existing BMS monitoring software to track inter-cell temperature differences

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: Standard requires BMS logic config (0.5 hr). Proposed adds sensor installation (0.3 hr) and algorithm programming (0.2 hr) – total 1.0 hr (higher but justified by physics)
- Commissioning: Standard practice (0.2 hr) vs proposed (0.2 hr) – same
- Operation: No change – uses existing 1 A balancing current
- Maintenance: Same as standard – no additional components
- Cost class: Sensors are commodity items; software modification is within existing BMS capability

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Cycle module at 1C charge/discharge with 15°C gradient for 1,000 cycles; measure cell voltage spreads weekly.
Instruments: Existing BMS voltage monitoring + thermocouples (as installed)
Pass criterion: Voltage spread remains <35 mV at all measurement points
Kill criterion: Spread exceeds 35 mV for 3 consecutive cycles
Duration: 1,000 cycles (~6 months at accelerated aging)
Validation: Compare against control module with standard balancing; intervention module must show statistically significant reduction in spread growth rate.
